Taste 60+ Jeju Products at Resorts World Sentosa, Then Have Them Delivered
 Danish Lukawski October 30, 2026 4 minutes read

 ’26 Meet Jeju in Singapore runs from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Resorts World Sentosa , bringing more than 60 products from South Korea’s largest island to Sentosa for three days. You can sample things like camellia sunscreen and tangerine coffee, then scan a QR code to order them on Lazada or Shopee for home delivery, so nobody has to lug a shopping bag back onto the monorail.
 This is the third edition, hosted by the Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Jeju Business Agency (JBA) . The organisers say more than 20 brands will bring food, seafood, drinks, cosmetics and lifestyle products, and many of them are making their Singapore debut. Products from 22 participating Jeju companies will be on Lazada and Shopee, which matters most if you can’t spare a weekday on Sentosa.
 Sample It, Scan It, Ship It
 The main stop is the Jeju Premium Products Global Promotion Pavilion , open daily from 10am to 8pm . According to the event details, it is at WEAVE, Level 1, Villa C. You browse, you taste, and if something wins you over, you scan its QR code and check out on Lazada or Shopee. The platforms deliver it to your door.
 It’s a sensible fix for the classic pop-up problem of falling for a snack and then never finding it again. If you’ve ever stacked vouchers during a Shopee sale , the checkout will feel familiar. The difference is that here you get to taste the product before you add it to your cart.
 There’s a party on day one too. On 4 November from 3pm to 6pm , the public launch at the B1 WEAVE atrium has interactive games, lucky draws with Jeju products as prizes, and Korean dance performances. Arrive early if you want a good spot for the dance performances!
 Snacks, Seafood and Tangerine Coffee
 Fissueh’s Purung Badang fishcake is steamed from Alaska pollock surimi rather than fried, so it’s lighter and less oily than the usual kind.
 The brand with the best story is Jeju Basalt , a company founded in 2018 that makes food shaped like the island’s volcanic rock. Its Jeju Basalt Cake has a 10-day best-before at room temperature, so it’s one to eat soon rather than keep.
 If you’re thinking about gifts, the Jeju Mandarin Drip Coffee is the smarter pick. It won silver at the 23rd Jeju Tourism Souvenir Contest. Social enterprise Jejumami brings Hokklak Chips , roasted brown rice chips that come in a tangerine version. Hokklak is Jeju dialect for “small and cute”, according to the company.
 For something heartier, JeBada Jeju Seafood’s Abalone & Sea Snail Chowder comes ready-packed. It’s the kind of thing you’d want in the cupboard for a rainy-season dinner.
 Beauty Picks Worth Scanning
 Our first pick is the JejuIndi Camellia Blossom Sun Cream . It’s SPF 50+ (sun protection factor) with 10% Jeju camellia flower extract, and the brand says it leaves no white cast. In Singapore, where sunscreen is a daily habit, that claim alone is worth testing at the booth.
 The Accoje Reviving Green Cica Care Serum, from UCL’s skincare brand made in Jeju with Jeju ingredients Our second pick is the PARANG PARAN Intensive Bio-Cellulose Mask from the Jeju Institute of Perfumery. It’s a vegan sheet mask made with Jeju lava seawater, and the brand recommends using it about once a week for around an hour. The same institute makes ASRAHAN Eau de Parfum Janon , which opens with Jeju pine and settles into cedarwood and powdery musk. Perfume is hard to judge from a product page, which makes it a good thing to sniff at the pavilion before you scan.
 UCL Co., Ltd. brings its Reviving Sleeping Mask with Jeju honey and propolis. The rest of the list includes BETTERSKIN shampoo , which uses Jeju volcanic ash, and Unijeju’s Golden Prestige Collection . If skincare tech is your thing, our look at L’Oréal’s beauty innovations is a good companion read.
 The S$20 Beef Bonus
 This is the perk to plan around. The first 350 visitors who spend S$20 or more on Jeju products at the event get complimentary tasting vouchers for Jeju Hanwoo beef and black pork at DRIM Gold .
 Marbled Hanwoo cuts from Salt by Peb, one of the Jeju beef producers bringing Korea’s native cattle to Singapore Hanwoo is Korea’s native cattle breed. For a S$20 spend on sunscreen or snacks, a taste of beef is a very good deal!
 Why Jeju Keeps Coming Back
 The event also covers travel and study. The Jeju Tourism Organization will introduce NOWDA, Jeju’s tourism membership programme, alongside prize giveaways and promotional videos. Separately, the Jeju Free International City Development Center will host international education institutions.
 “Our goal is not only to showcase the quality of Jeju products, but also to turn consumer interest into purchases and lasting business partnerships,” said Ko Hi Shin , Director of the Jeju Business Agency Singapore Representative Office. The sample-then-scan setup is built around that aim, which works out well for shoppers who’d rather not carry their haul home.
 🗓️ Date: 4 to 6 November 2026 (Wednesday to Friday)
⏰ Time: 10am to 8pm daily (product exhibition and food tasting)
📍 Location: Jeju Premium Products Global Promotion Pavilion, WEAVE, Level 1, Villa C, Resorts World Sentosa, 26 Sentosa Gateway, Singapore 098138
🎉 Public launch: 4 November, 3pm to 6pm, B1 WEAVE atrium, with games, lucky draws and Korean dance performances
🛒 Shopping: Scan QR codes to buy on Lazada and Shopee, with home delivery through the platforms
🥩 Perk: Tasting vouchers for Jeju Hanwoo beef and black pork at DRIM Gold for the first 350 visitors who spend S$20 or more
🎟️ Entry: Open to the public
 Go for the camellia sunscreen, take home the tangerine coffee, and get your S$20 in early before the vouchers run out. The full product range and updates are on the Jeju Business Agency’s ASEAN website , and the team posts behind-the-scenes looks on Jeju ASEAN’s Instagram , so follow along before you head to Sentosa!
